metadata.review_scope: Phase 1 governance path, scope, secret, environment security mechanisms only

findings.evidence: A manifest-listed evidence artifact records an absolute workstation path to a .dump file. Additional absolute local paths occur at docs/migration-320-before-after.json:26, docs/migration-320-before-after.json:1940, docs/migration-320-before-after.json:1941, docs/migration-320-before-after.json:1946, docs/migration-320-before-after.json:1952 and docs/migration-320-before-after.json:2103; docs/cross-module-closure-report.md:3 and docs/migration-320-compatibility-report.md:52 also record absolute local paths. The artifact is included by .codex/tasks/GOV-M320-DRYRUN/artifact-manifest.yaml:6 and is content-scanned without an absolute-path rule by .codex/scripts/lib/secret-scanner.mjs:4-10.
findings.reproduction: From the product root, run the scoped read-only search used by this review for drive-letter and UNC forms over AGENTS.md, .codex, .agents, and the five manifest-listed docs; observe the cited matches. No .env file is searched or read.
findings.impact: The governance evidence violates the requirement that governance artifacts add no absolute local paths, exposes workstation/user/directory layout, preserves references to dump artifacts, and is non-portable. Because these files are hash-bound evidence, sanitization also requires manifest hash regeneration and revalidation before acceptance.

findings.evidence: validate-task scans manifest-listed artifact content at lines 229-235 and required Task files at lines 237-237, but it does not scan the complete governance corpus (.codex scripts, policies, agents, templates, workflows, .agents skill, or all governance docs). The scanner patterns at .codex/scripts/lib/secret-scanner.mjs:4-10 omit absolute local paths and many credential families/encoded secrets. The limitation is acknowledged at .codex/governance/residual-risks.yaml:16.
findings.reproduction: Place a drive-letter path or an unsupported token family in a temporary governance fixture outside the fixture artifact manifest and invoke validateTask against that fixture; validation has no corpus-wide rule that reports it. The present scoped search independently found SEC-A-001 while validate-task reported the dry run structurally valid.
findings.impact: A structurally valid Task can retain sensitive or machine-specific strings outside the narrow scan set, so the validator cannot substantiate a governance-wide no-secret/no-local-path claim.

findings.evidence: The scope validator unions repository-wide staged, unstaged and untracked paths at lines 83-88 and validates all of them against one Task's allowed_write_paths. The current read-only invocation for GOV-M320-DRYRUN failed on numerous pre-existing governance and product changes outside that Task. The success message itself limits proof to changed-files-only and states branch_or_worktree_restriction=false at line 91.
findings.reproduction: Run node .codex/scripts/validate-change-scope.mjs --task-id GOV-M320-DRYRUN from the product root. It reports OUTSIDE_TASK_SCOPE for unrelated dirty-worktree files from the staged/unstaged/untracked union.
findings.impact: The gate fails closed, which is safer than accepting mixed changes, but it cannot attribute changes to this Task or produce a usable positive scope attestation in the current shared dirty worktree. Human-controlled isolation/pathspec review remains required before Git mutation.

findings.evidence: The path helper performs segment-by-segment lstat and realpath checks and rejects stat.isSymbolicLink(), then revalidates after creation. It does not hold directory handles across check/use operations and cannot eliminate replacement races; the residual is accurately recorded at .codex/governance/residual-risks.yaml:13. Its error text groups all reparse-point forms with links although the code predicate is isSymbolicLink() at line 33.
findings.reproduction: Review safeNewPath at lines 60-66 followed by caller write/mkdir and verifyCreatedPath. There is necessarily a check/use interval. The approved fixture rejects traversal, absolute, graph escape and a junction, but does not prove immunity to every Windows reparse type or concurrent replacement.
findings.impact: Under a concurrently writable or hostile workspace, path components may change between validation and use. Phase 1 must retain this as a residual risk and must not represent the path policy as an OS sandbox.

checks.evidence: .codex/scripts/lib/path-safety.mjs:27-42 checks each existing segment with lstat and realpath; canonical containment is enforced. TOCTOU and non-link reparse coverage remain residual per SEC-A-004.
.codex/scripts/lib/path-safety.mjs:10-19 rejects empty, traversal, absolute, drive-letter, UNC and .env segments; governance fixture case 12 rejected traversal, absolute and graph escape.
Governance fixture case 12 rejected a junction; the scoped live tree enumeration found no ReparsePoint attributes. General Windows reparse/TOCTOU assurance is limited as recorded in SEC-A-004.
.codex/scripts/create-task.mjs:30-33 and :52-57 validate before creation and revalidate after creation. The interval is not atomic.
.codex/scripts/validate-task.mjs:284-291 resolves graph source_ref through safeExistingPath; governance fixture case 12 rejected graph escape.
.codex/scripts/validate-change-scope.mjs:83-91 collects all three sets and fails closed. Current replay fails because unrelated changes are mixed; see SEC-A-003.

.codex/meta-rules/global.yaml:6 and .codex/governance/residual-risks.yaml:10 reserve mutation operations to humans, but no command hook, branch protection, CODEOWNERS, required-review or CI evidence exists.
.codex/governance/agent-path-policy.yaml:3-4 declares commit-time-role-scope-gate and runtime_isolation=false; .codex/governance/residual-risks.yaml:12 repeats the limitation.
Known patterns are scanned in manifest and required Task content, but governance-wide coverage and absolute-local-path detection are absent; actual violations are recorded in SEC-A-001 and SEC-A-002.

.codex/scripts/lib/secret-scanner.mjs:13-17 rejects dump/backup suffixes and non-text artifacts unless authority is approved-binary. No binary file was found in the scoped governance artifact list, but manifest evidence contains absolute strings referencing .dump files.

.codex/scripts/validate-agent-environment.mjs:29-38 enforces no dotenv, explicit JSON source, loopback, port 5433, rehearsal naming/mode, no operations and no secret-like keys. The safe profile contains no credentials.

.codex/scripts/validate-agent-environment.mjs:44-56 and .codex/governance/environment-safety-evidence.json:40-46 explicitly state runtime command isolation, OS env denial and product-script integration are false.
.codex/governance/residual-risks.yaml:6-9 records child_process, PowerShell, cmd.exe, arbitrary external executable and Parent permission override bypass risks; no enforcement mechanism closes them.
Read-only source execution using temporary fixtures completed 21/21 cases, including no-overwrite, path escape/junction, scope, secret, review identity, approval and gate cases.
validate-task replay returned structural=VALID and calculated_gate=NO-GO with the expected evidence, review, blocker and approval reasons.
PowerShell read-only attribute enumeration over AGENTS.md, .codex, .agents and the five manifest-listed docs returned no ReparsePoint entries.

limitations: The review did not read any .env file or its contents.
The review did not read frontend, erp-api, db-design or migration source; only the five docs explicitly listed by GOV-M320-DRYRUN were read under docs evidence authority.

No service, product test, database command, database connection, Git mutation, branch operation, commit, worktree operation or external executable beyond Node, Git read commands and PowerShell read-only inspection was performed.
The review is a filesystem and governance-mechanism assessment, not proof of Codex runtime context isolation or OS sandbox enforcement.
The scoped content scan uses deterministic patterns and cannot establish absence of every encoded, fragmented or novel secret.
Git hosting controls and remote repository policy were not available as local evidence.
No adversarial concurrent filesystem race was attempted; TOCTOU assessment is code-based.
The current dirty worktree prevents a clean per-Task positive change-scope attestation without human-controlled isolation or an approved baseline/provenance mechanism.
